changes.after: Choose how a Label looks when shown or inspected.

before: str(value) asks for a readable string, often for display. repr(value) asks for a developer-oriented representation. A class can define __str__ and __repr__ to control these operations. Both methods must return strings; printing inside them is not a substitute for returning.

Label stores a supplied string. __str__ returns that text. __repr__ returns a class-like label containing the represented text. In an f-string, !r applies repr to the embedded value, preserving visible quotes or escapes that plain display can hide.

The calls str(item) and repr(item) invoke the corresponding special methods. print(item) normally uses the readable string too. A representation can be useful for debugging without being a safe expression to execute; never eval an untrusted representation.
Implement Label so str(instance) returns its text and repr(instance) returns Label(...) containing repr(text). Treat text as a string. Return strings without printing inside either special method.
after:
`str(value)` asks for readable text to show a person. `repr(value)` asks for text that helps you inspect the value while fixing code.

A class can define `__str__` and `__repr__` to choose that text. Both methods must return a string. Printing a message inside them is not enough.

Our `Label` stores a string. Its `__str__` method returns that text. Its `__repr__` method puts `repr(text)` inside `Label(...)`.

Inside an f-string, `!r` uses `repr` on the value. This can show quotes or backslashes that ordinary display hides.

`str(item)` and `repr(item)` use the matching special methods. `print(item)` normally uses the readable text too.

Text from `repr` helps you inspect a value. It is not always code you can safely run. `eval` runs text as code, so do not use it on text you do not trust.

Build `Label`. `str(instance)` should return its saved text. `repr(instance)` should return `Label(...)` with `repr(text)` inside.

The supplied text is a string. Return the answers from both methods; do not just print them.
